* **The Formula:** $J = F_{\text{avg}} \times \Delta t = \Delta p$

  * $J$: Impulse, the push or hit delivered over time (measured in $\text{N}\cdot\text{s}$ or $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$)
  * $F_{\text{avg}}$: Average force, the steady push applied during the collision (measured in newtons)
  * $\Delta t$: Time interval, how long the force acts (measured in seconds)
  * $\Delta p$: Change in momentum, the difference between final and initial momentum
* **Why we use it:** The area under a force-time graph adds up all the little $F\,\Delta t$ contributions. This total tells us how much the object's momentum changed during the interaction, which is exactly what impulse measures.

🎯 **Exam Tip:** In DBE Physical Sciences exams, this is typically a 1-mark question. Always write the full word "Impulse" — do not just write $J$ or $\Delta p$, as the memo looks for the named physical quantity.
